question: Why prices rise when the government increases spending or cuts taxes?

options.text: Firm not be able to produce higher quantities that are being demanded at ongoing prices.
Firm exports their produces to the foreign destinations

solution:
The correct answer is __**Firm not be able to produce higher quantities that are being demanded at ongoing prices.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• **Government Spending and Aggregate Demand:** When the government **increases spending** or **cuts taxes**, it boosts aggregate demand in the economy. People and businesses have more money to spend, leading to an increase in the overall demand for goods and services. 
• **Firm's Production Capacity:** Firms may not be able to **immediately increase their production** to match the higher demand at current prices. This is because production capacities are often limited by resources, machinery, or labor availability. 
• **Price Rise:** When demand surpasses the available supply and firms cannot produce more in the short term, **prices rise**. This phenomenon is known as demand-pull inflation.
